harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented node2↔node3 traffic shaping through VyOS router node1 via an Ansible playbook run from control node4. node2 (lan-a, 10.10.10.0/24) and node3 (lan-b, 10.10.20.0/24) got static IPs on their second NIC via nmcli plus routes to each other's subnet via node1. node1 got static addresses on eth1/eth2 and a VyOS qos shaper policy (HTB, 1mbit) applied as an egress policy on eth2 (facing node3), capping all node2→node3 traffic to 1 Mbit/s while eth1 (facing node2) stays unshaped for the reverse direction. Verified with iperf3: node2→node3 settled at ~1.04 Mbit/s, node3→node2 reached ~1.5+ Gbit/s unrestricted. All four nodes were restarted one at a time with boot_id changes proving real reboots, and all state (static IPs, routes, VyOS shaper config) was confirmed to persist. Caught and fixed a reconciler gotcha: an ad-hoc SSH key drop into VyOS's authorized_keys file was wiped on reboot by VyOS's login reconciler; replaced with a proper `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config entry which persisted, and re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency and full recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology via environment.toml: node1=VyOS router with eth0(mgmt)/eth1(lan-a)/eth2(lan-b), node2=AlmaLinux eth0(mgmt)/eth1(lan-a), node3=AlmaLinux eth0(mgmt)/eth1(lan-b), node4=Ubuntu control node with ansible-core installed
Set up passwordless cluster SSH (cluster_ed25519 key) from node4 to root@node2, root@node3, and vyos@node1 with passwordless sudo to root

Diagnosed VyOS quirk: the configure/commit/save alias-based CLI session only initializes correctly when the script runs as root (sudo), not as the vyos user directly - fixed by using ansible_become=sudo on the vyos host
Built /root/ansible/{ansible.cfg,inventory.ini,site.yml} on node4 defining lan_endpoints (node2,node3) and vyos_router (node1) groups
Playbook: configured static IPv4 on node2/node3's eth1 via community.general.nmcli plus a route to the peer's LAN subnet via node1's gateway IP; installed iperf3 for testing

Playbook: pushed VyOS config on node1 setting eth1=10.10.10.1/24, eth2=10.10.20.1/24, and a qos policy shaper LIMIT-TO-NODE3 (bandwidth 1mbit, default class 100%) applied as egress policy on eth2 only
Ran the playbook successfully (idempotent on re-run), verified interface addresses, routes, and tc qdisc (htb on eth2, plain fq_codel on eth1)

Verified traffic shaping empirically with iperf3: node2->node3 throughput capped near 1 Mbit/s; node3->node2 throughput unrestricted (~1.5+ Gbit/s); opened/closed firewalld port 5201 on node2/node3 for the test only

Executed mandatory restart protocol on all 4 nodes sequentially (node1, node2, node3, node4): captured boot_id + health baseline, issued a deferred `reboot`, polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified recovered state (IPs, routes, VyOS shaper config) after each restart

After node1's reboot, the re-run playbook failed because the manually-appended SSH key in /home/vyos/.ssh/authorized_keys had been regenerated by VyOS's login reconciler; fixed by adding the key through `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` in VyOS config (persists across reboots) and re-verified idempotent playbook run

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 reach each other only through node1 (separate private networks, static addressing since dhcp=false)
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run shows changed=3 on node2/node3 applying static IPs (10.10.10.2/24, 10.10.20.2/24) and cross-subnet routes via node1; post-run `ip addr`/`ip route` on both nodes confirm the addresses and routes via 10.10.10.1/10.10.20.1

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured as router with static IPs on eth1/eth2, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Playbook task 'Push VyOS configuration' returned changed:[node1]; config.boot on node1 shows eth1=10.10.10.1/24 and eth2=10.10.20.1/24 persisted

evidence.requirement: Traffic from node2 toward node3 limited to 1 Mbit/s
evidence.summary: tc qdisc show on node1 eth2 shows htb root qdisc from the qos shaper policy; iperf3 test from node2 to node3 settled at ~1.04 Mbit/s sender / 953 Kbit/s receiver, matching the configured 1mbit cap

evidence.requirement: Traffic from node3 toward node2 left unrestricted
evidence.summary: tc qdisc show on node1 eth1 (facing node2) shows only plain fq_codel, no shaping class; iperf3 test from node3 to node2 reached ~1.5-2 Gbit/s with zero retransmits, confirming no cap in the reverse direction

evidence.requirement: Implementation done via Ansible from the designated control_node (node4)
evidence.summary: All configuration (nmcli static IP/routes on node2/node3, VyOS interface+QoS config on node1) was applied through a single ansible-playbook run executed on node4 (environment.toml control_node), and re-run cleanly afterward confirming idempotency

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7668189d.../uptime 653s baseline; issued deferred reboot; polled through connection timeouts/resets; new boot_id 4ae261b5... at uptime 22s proves a real reboot; post-restart eth1/eth2 addresses and the qos shaper (htb on eth2) were confirmed intact

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 513c865e.../uptime 635s baseline; issued deferred reboot; new boot_id f1214831... at uptime 4.07s proves reboot; post-restart static IP, route to 10.10.20.0/24, and successful ping to node3 confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 15443601.../uptime 635s baseline; issued deferred reboot; new boot_id a4715803... at uptime 4.41s proves reboot; post-restart static IP, route to 10.10.10.0/24, and successful ping to node2 confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node4 (control node) baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id c030bd0d.../uptime 636s baseline and confirmed ansible playbook files present; issued deferred reboot; new boot_id 195f87a8... at uptime 5s proves reboot; post-restart the ansible project files, SSH key, and /etc/hosts entries were intact, and a fresh ansible-playbook run completed successfully (after fixing the VyOS SSH-key reconciler issue), proving full functional recovery of the control node
